title: Donation thank-you and receipts
problem: Donors to a small Muslim charity wait days for a thank-you and a receipt while a volunteer copies each gift into a spreadsheet by hand. Zakat, Sadaqah, Waqf and general gifts need to be kept apart, and mistakes in the fund column are hard to spot later.
solution: Each new form row gets a receipt number built from the row number and a branded thank-you email with wording for its fund. Every gift is logged to a ledger with the fund kept in its own column. A weekly summary goes to the treasurer and a second trustee, one line per fund, with no AI anywhere in the flow.
human_check: Gifts of 1,000 or more, gifts with an unrecognised fund and gifts with no email go to a trustee, and the Zakat wording is to be confirmed with the charity's Shariah adviser.
linkedin_post:
A donor gives Zakat on Friday night and hears nothing until Wednesday.

That gap is common in small charities. One volunteer, one spreadsheet, a pile of gifts to copy across.

So I built a demo for a fictional charity, Crescent Hope Foundation, using sample data only. Each new donation gets a receipt number and a thank-you email within minutes. The wording changes by fund. Zakat donors are told their gift is kept in a separate account and goes only to eligible recipients. Waqf donors are told the principal is preserved and only the returns are spent. Every gift lands in a ledger with the fund in its own column, and the treasurer and a second trustee get a weekly summary, one line per fund.

This one uses no AI. Rules are cheaper and more predictable here.

The safeguard: large gifts, unclear fund types and missing emails go to a trustee, and the Zakat wording should be checked with the charity's Shariah adviser.

Blueprint and sample files are in the comments.
